Rubroboletus satanas hat einen blassen, schmutzig-weißen Hut, blutrote Poren und einen knolligen roten Stiel, und er läuft im Schnitt blau an. Der Satansröhrling, auch Satanspilz genannt, wächst auf Kalkböden unter Buchen und Eichen und verursacht heftiges Erbrechen; dem deutschen Mykologen Harald Othmar Lenz, der ihn 1831 beschrieb und benannte, wurde dabei von seinen Ausdünstungen übel.

| Pilz | Lateinischer Name | Benannt nach |
|---|---|---|
| der Parasol | Macrolepiota procera | einem Sonnenschirm |
| der Fliegenpilz | Amanita muscaria | Fliegen |
| der Austernseitling | Pleurotus ostreatus | Austern |
| das Judasohr | Auricularia auricula-judae | Judas Iskariot |
| der Satansröhrling | Rubroboletus satanas | dem Teufel |

Jeder Name ist eine winzige Geschichte, und die Geschichten sind oft leichter zu merken als das Latein.

sets.articleEn:
The internet of the early 2000s was built by small groups of friends in rented rooms, and the names on the founding documents have become as familiar as the logos. The company in the original question started as a side project inside a failing one. In 2006 the podcasting start-up Odeo, run by Evan Williams and Noah Glass, was being overtaken by Apple's iTunes, and during a brainstorming session the engineer Jack Dorsey proposed a service for sending short status messages by text message to a group of friends. Glass came up with the name, Biz Stone helped build the prototype, and the first message, „just setting up my twttr“, was sent on 21 March 2006. Twitter was spun out as its own company the following year, its 140-character limit was inherited from the length of an SMS, and by the 2010s it had become the medium in which news broke. Elon Musk bought it in 2022 and renamed it X in 2023.

The founders' habit of starting in a garage is older. Larry Page and Sergey Brin met as doctoral students at Stanford in 1995 and built a search engine, first called BackRub, that ranked pages by the links pointing to them. They incorporated Google on 4 September 1998 in the garage of Susan Wojcicki in Menlo Park; the name is a misspelling of „googol“, the number 1 followed by 100 zeros. Since 2015 the company has been a subsidiary of the holding Alphabet.

Facebook began in a Harvard dormitory. Mark Zuckerberg launched „Thefacebook“ on 4 February 2004 with his roommates Dustin Moskovitz and Chris Hughes, the programmer Andrew McCollum and the business student Eduardo Saverin, who put up the first money. It was restricted to Harvard students, then to other universities, and opened to everyone in 2006. The company changed its name to Meta in 2021.

YouTube was founded by three former PayPal employees, Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim, on 14 February 2005; the story goes that they could not find a way to share videos of a dinner party. The first clip, „Me at the zoo“, shows Karim in front of the elephants in San Diego. Google bought YouTube for 1.65 billion dollars in November 2006, only eighteen months later.

Instagram was the smallest team of all. Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger, two Stanford graduates, launched the photo-sharing app for the iPhone on 6 October 2010 after stripping down a location-based check-in service called Burbn to its most popular feature, the filtered photo. It reached a million users in two months and was bought by Facebook for one billion dollars in April 2012, when it still had thirteen employees.

|---|---|---|
| Google | 1998 | Larry Page, Sergey Brin |
| Facebook | 2004 | Mark Zuckerberg, Eduardo Saverin, Dustin Moskovitz, Chris Hughes, Andrew McCollum |
| YouTube | 2005 | Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim |
| Twitter | 2006 | Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone, Evan Williams |

Five companies, twelve years and fewer than twenty founders: between them they defined how a generation searches, shares and argues online.

September 1998 gründeten sie Google in der Garage von Susan Wojcicki in Menlo Park; der Name ist eine Falschschreibung von „Googol“, der Zahl 1 mit 100 Nullen.
